exercise.name: Band Horizontal Pallof Press

reference.title: Band Horizontal Pallof Press
reference.listing: Video (movement reference; the page could not be fetched from the authoring environment, so the data sheet was not read; the movement follows the exercise name and standard coaching)

exercise.mechanics: Isometric trunk (anti-rotation) with a horizontal arm press

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as you press the hands out, breathe steadily (short breaths) while you hold, breathe in as the hands come back to the chest.
breathing.cadence: About 1 s out, 1.5 s hold, 1 s back

prescription.reps: 8-12 per side with a 1-3 s hold, or timed holds of 10-30 s
prescription.effort: Stop when the trunk starts to turn toward the anchor (clinical opinion)
prescription.load: Band tension is user-chosen: step farther from the anchor for more tension
prescription.progression: Longer holds, a stronger band, a step farther from the anchor, a narrower stance, then half-kneeling or split stance

cues.text: Stand side-on to the anchor, band at chest height, feet about shoulder width, knees soft. Hold the band handle in both hands against the middle of the chest.
Brace and press the hands straight out from the chest; do not let the band turn you toward the anchor.
Hold with the arms long, hands in line with the breastbone; hips and shoulders stay square to the front.
Bring the hands back to the chest slowly, still square.
Short pause at the chest, then press again. Turn around to train the other side.

mistakes.mistake: Trunk or hips turning toward the anchor
mistakes.fix: Brace harder, step closer to the anchor or use a lighter band.

mistakes.mistake: Pressing up or across instead of straight out
mistakes.fix: Hands travel straight out from the breastbone at chest height.
Shoulders down and back; the arms do little work.

mistakes.mistake: Leaning away from the band or shifting onto one foot
mistakes.fix: Weight even on both feet, ribs stacked over the pelvis.
Breathe out on the press and keep breathing in short breaths through the hold.

kinematics.norm: None: the task is to resist the band's turning pull (anti-rotation; clinical opinion)
From the chest straight out to about arm's length at chest height (clinical opinion)
Elbows bent at the chest, nearly straight at the end (clinical opinion)
Feet about shoulder width, knees soft; a narrower stance or kneeling is harder (clinical opinion)
Slow press, hold of a few seconds (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual, Band Horizontal Pallof Press, video (movement reference)
Oliva-Lozano and Muyor 2020, core muscle activity during physical fitness exercises: a systematic review (Int J Environ Res Public Health 17(12):4306)
McGill 1998, low back exercises: evidence for improving exercise regimens (Phys Ther 78(7):754-765; PMID 9672547)
Torso-twist exercise with elastic resistance vs a training machine: core muscle EMG (Scientifica 2015:403068; PubMed 26557405)

cautions: Stop if you feel sharp, radiating or nerve-type pain.
Check the band and the anchor before each set: a band that slips or snaps can hit you.
Band tension is user-chosen: pick one you can hold without turning.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Shoulder discomfort: keep the hands closer to the chest (shorter lever).
Low back discomfort: soften the knees a little more and keep the ribs down over the pelvis.
regressions: Lighter band or stand closer to the anchor.
Hands stay at the chest (isometric hold only).
progressions: Overhead (vertical) press from the extended position.

muscleNotes.obliques_r: Resist the band's turning pull. Anti-rotation work loads the obliques isometrically; no peer-reviewed EMG data for this exact press were found, so activation follows elastic torso-twist data (external oblique about 54-77% MVC in dynamic twists, Scientifica 2015) scaled down for an isometric hold (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Resist the band's turning pull (the oblique pair works across the trunk; clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.core: Rectus and transversus abdominis brace the trunk so the ribs stay over the pelvis (McGill 1998 describes bracing for spine stability).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Keep the spine tall and resist the small sideways and turning pull (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Keep the spine tall and resist the small sideways and turning pull (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Keep the pelvis level and square to the front (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_med_l: Keep the pelvis level and square to the front (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Hold the arms out in front (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Hold the arms out in front (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.pec_r: Press the hands out and hold them in line with the breastbone (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.pec_l: Press the hands out and hold them in line with the breastbone (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Keep the shoulder blades on the rib cage as the arms reach (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.serratus_l: Keep the shoulder blades on the rib cage as the arms reach (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Light squeeze keeps the hips under the trunk (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Light squeeze keeps the hips under the trunk (clinical opinion).

guides.label: Hands press straight out from the chest
